name: Charpy ISO-V impact energy and lateral expansion of austenitic stainless (304L/316L) LNG weld metal at -196 C (ASTM E23; ASME 0.38 mm / TUV 32 J acceptance)
plain_name: Qualify stainless-steel welds for LNG tanks by checking a notched weld sample still absorbs impact at -196 C
description: Weld metal and joints made with low-ferrite 308L/316L consumables (SMAW, GTAW, FCAW) are Charpy V-notch tested per ASTM E23 at -196 C, the LNG qualification temperature, and also at +20 and -120 C; lateral expansion is checked against the ASME B31.3 minimum of 0.38 mm and impact energy against the TUV minimum of 32 J.
keywords: Qualify stainless-steel welds for LNG tanks by checking a notched weld sample still absorbs impact at -196 C

sources.citation: Welding of austenitic stainless steels for cryogenic LNG applications - Low Temperature Behaviour of Austenitic Weldments (Friedrich, Posch, Tosch, Ziegerhofer, Berger; Boehler Welding Austria)

requirements.rationale: The qualification test temperature for LNG weldments is -196 C; specimens must be conditioned at -196 C (77.15 K).
Optional: the full toughness-versus-temperature curves were measured at +20, -120 and -196 C.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
